title: Syncing Apple Music across your devices is easier than you think

claims.claim: Apple Music is available on multiple platforms including Android phones, Windows PCs, and smart TVs.

evidence.quote: You can, for example, sign in with your Apple Account and listen to your favorite songs on an Android phone, Windows PC or even smart TVs.

claims.claim: To check the account on Apple Music, open the app and tap the profile picture on the Home tab.

evidence.quote: If you're not sure which account you're using, open the Apple Music app and tap your profile picture on the Home tab.

claims.claim: On an iPhone or iPad, Sync Library can be enabled by going to Settings, finding Apps, and selecting the Music app.

evidence.quote: On your iPhone or iPad, open Settings and look for Apps. Then, find the Music app in the list and enable Sync Library.

claims.claim: On a Mac, Sync Library is found under Settings in the General tab of the Music app.

evidence.quote: On a Mac, open the Music app and click the "Music" menu at the top of the screen, then go to Settings. Now, under the General tab, make sure Sync Library is enabled and click OK to save your settings.
On a Mac, open the Music app and click the "Music" menu at the top of the screen, then go to Settings. Now, under the General tab, make sure Sync Library is enabled

claims.claim: On Android phones, the Sync Library option is enabled by default.

evidence.quote: If you have an Android phone, this option is enabled by default, and you don't need to change anything.

claims.claim: In the Mac and Windows Apple Music apps, users can select Update Cloud Library to force the app to sync.

evidence.quote: In the Mac app, click the File menu, then go to Library and select Update Cloud Library — this will force the app to sync and check for updates in your personal library. This option is also available in the Windows app and can be found in the sidebar.

claims.claim: Android and iOS apps do not have the Update Cloud Library option.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, the Android and iOS apps don't have that option.

claims.claim: Users can change audio quality options in Apple Music to enable lossless audio.

evidence.quote: While you're there, it's worth exploring some other toggles, like changing the audio quality options to enable lossless audio.
